segments.he: וזה גלמי ראו עיניך ועל ספרך כולם יכתבו ימים יוצרו ולו אחד בהם זה יוה"כ כנ"ל. גלמי ראו עיניך שהראה הקב"ה לאדם הראשון דור דור ודורשיטו וכו' כשרז"ל והראה לו במה יתקיים העולם באחרית הימים האלה בעיקבות משיחא והראה לו שעתה קיום התורה שהואקיום העולם הוא על ידי ריבוי הספרים הקדושים שנתרבין ע"י חותם דקודשה שהוא מלאכת הדפוס כנ"ל. וזה ועל ספרך כולם יכתבו כולם דייקא שכל החידושין של הצדיקים כולם יהיו נכתבין על ספריך כי עכשיו נתכב הכל בביאור היטב ע"י מלאכת הדפוס כנ"ל שעל ידי זה נשלם תורה שבכתב ותורה שבע"פ שע"י זהנתתקנין הדמים שבשס"ה גידין שזהו בחינת יוה"כ ענ"ל וזהו ועל ספרך כולם יכתבו ימים יוצרו ולו אחד בהם זה יוה"כ כי הם בחינת אחת כנ"ל:
segments.en:
Theme: The final installment weaves together counting and number, the census of Israel, handwashing, the fire-kashering of vessels, Moshe's final prayer, Dovid's yahrzeit, the dispute of Korach — and concludes with a magnificent exposition on the concept of pesach (opening/channel) as the essential mechanism of all spiritual drawing, all holiness, all life, and all death. Tzitzis, mezuza, skin afflictions, and the opening of the earth to swallow Korach are all revealed as aspects of this single principle.

§39: G-d's counting of the days of creation encodes the koach/po'al principle. Number (mispar) only becomes applicable once things have moved from potential to actuality. The essential rectification: returning the plurality back to the One without nullifying the world — the ratzo vashuv of Ezekiel's living creatures. The omer-count is the rectification of number before Shavuos — seven weeks corresponding to the seven days of creation — reconnecting all plurality to its root.

§40: The portion of Bamidbar (counting of Israel) precedes Shavuos for this reason: a great multitude of students is needed to receive the pi shnayim from the tzadik, since more holy vessels can receive more light. But this requires ahavas chavayrim (love of companions) — otherwise the sitra achra gains hold through the very multiplicity. The half-shekel = the two yuds. Tzedakah draws the opening from above to below. Dispute within Israel is the greatest obstacle of all. Eliyahu's role: to restore the heart of fathers to children = ruach dil'ayla returning to ruach dil'tata. Ten for a minyan = the Yud — the quorum that can draw from upper Yud to lower Yud.

§41: Handwashing before meals — the water derives from the mikveh waters where the spirit of Mashiach hovers. The hands are the instruments of koach v'po'al (right and left, potential and actuality). All human activity is accomplished through hands. Therefore impurity and purity are bound to them above all. Handwashing before eating = purifying the primary instrument of actualization before the act of drawing vitality.

§42: Handwashing before prayer — especially morning handwashing upon waking. Night/sleep = the darkness of obstacles, which deposit the ruach ra'ah most powerfully on the hands. Morning handwashing purifies the hands to pray — for prayer is speech, and speech is the essential channel of koach el hapo'al. The Talmudic statement "it is as if he immersed" confirms: handwashing = mikveh immersion.

§43: Kashering non-Jewish vessels through fire — the halachic process is decoded. Fire-purging = the downfall of the wicked (the forbidden matter is the husk/wickedness; it was absorbed through the fire of desires and jealousy, so it is expelled through fire). The removal of rust before kashering = the removal of falsehood that covers truth. Gold and silver = supernal hues whose root is very high — corrupted when one becomes dependent on others and "changes his face." After fire-kashering (= downfall of wicked = perfection of speech), mikveh immersion draws the vowel-points that complete the letters of speech, and new holy spirit flows.

§44: Moshe's prayer for a successor: "Hashem, G-d of the ruchos" — the plural ruchos (spirits) refers to the two spirits of pi shnayim. The essential eternal rectification requires a tzadik to leave students who will continue drawing pi shnayim after his passing.

§45: The same formula — "G-d of the spirits" — appears when Moshe and Aharon fall on their faces during Korach's rebellion. The ruchos is the key: even the worst outbreak of dispute and heresy is healed through the few worthy students who draw pi shnayim from the tzadik. Moshe's plea: "one man sinned" — Korach was the instigator; the rest were led astray innocently, and the illumination of pi shnayim through the tzadik's students will eventually bring them all back to truth.

§46–47: Dovid died on Shavuos because his passing is what enables the annual drawing of pi shnayim for kabbalas haTorah — for the tzadik is most powerful after his histalkus. Dovid King of Israel lives and endures = his Torah continues to be drawn = that is his life. Song of Songs 3:4 ("scarcely had I passed by them") = Rashi: after Moshe's passing, the Land was conquered — tzadikim are greater in death than in life.

§48: A vessel not of that day cannot render food forbidden — the forbidden flavor is impaired after its time. The wicked have power only on their day. The persecuted must wait, pray, and study — for each morning a new sifting of truth from falsehood occurs (ma'asay Berayshis renewed daily), and this sifting is itself the gradual downfall of the wicked. Shema is fixed in the morning blessings of the luminaries because Shema = truth = the source of the luminaries' light. The stories of Sancheriv and Haman illustrate: the wicked's power was broken the very moment their day passed and the new day began.

§49–50: The opening of the earth to swallow Korach — the grand climax. The entire section on the pesach (opening/channel) is the deepest statement of the teaching: light is infinite and always desires to flow; it cannot be received directly; vessels/channels/contractions are needed; but they must not completely conceal the light — rather, a pesach (opening) must remain at each level through which light flows in graduated measure. This applies at every spiritual level — one must always make a new opening at a higher level. "Open for me the gates of righteousness" = the prayer for access to ever higher levels. "This is the gate of Hashem — tzadikim shall enter through it" = only the tzadikim can open these gates. Moshe's miracle: he opened an actual physical opening in the earth — demonstrating that the tzadik's power extends from the highest of heights to the lowest of earthly depths. Death and Resurrection: without sin, man would have made the opening himself and lived forever; because of sin, the soul must be refined through death, until Resurrection = G-d's opening of the grave. Korach denied the entire concept of the tzadik's power to open — therefore his punishment: the earth opened its mouth.

§51: Three questions of Korach — tzitzis, mezuza, and the bright patch of leprosy — are all aspects of the same heresy. A garment entirely of techeles: denying that you need channels/threads to receive infinite light in measured doses. A house full of books: denying that you need the specific opening of the mezuza. The bright patch: in impurity too there are openings — when the patch spreads over the entire body (parcha b'kulo tahor) the opening is nullified and it is pure. Non-Jews cannot defile through nega'im — because the laws of purity apply only where there is holiness to be protected and openings to be rectified. All commandments and transgressions depend on the opening: "You open Your hands" in holiness; and the dead are those "cut off from Your hand" — they blemished the opening. The entire Halacha ends by circling back to its beginning: Korach denied Moshe; Moshe's power is to make an opening from the height of all heights to the depth of all depths; the earth opened its mouth — and the truth was revealed.

Note from translator: §48 contains an extended excursus on daily siftings (bairurim) and the miracle of Sancheriv's downfall, citing Sanhedrin 95a, which belongs to a sub-theme of truth-revelation as the mechanism of the wicked's downfall — connecting the halachic rule of ayno ben yomo to a cosmic principle. §49 is among the longest and most philosophically dense sections in the entire halacha — comparable in depth to the great pesach-passage of Likutay Moharan I:66 itself. The term baheres k'gris (§51) refers to the Mishnah in Nega'im 8:3; the Zoharic phrase d'achlai kula v'shatzi kula (§51) is cited in the name of our master in Likutay Moharan I:49. The colophon chazak chazak v'nischazek is traditional at the conclusion of a book of the Torah; its appearance here marks the completion of Hechsher Kailim 4 and of the entire halacha.
